assertions.description: A 2D context created with {colorType: 'float16', toneMapping: {mode: 'extended'}} reports toneMapping.mode === 'extended' from getContextAttributes() — the only evidence the member was honoured rather than ignored.
assertions.test: (() => { const a = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d', { colorType: 'float16', toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' } }).getContextAttributes(); return !!a.toneMapping && a.toneMapping.mode === 'extended'; })()

assertions.description: Omitting toneMapping yields getContextAttributes().toneMapping.mode === 'standard' (the dictionary default, today's SDR behaviour).
Requesting {mode: 'standard'} explicitly is reported back as 'standard'.
assertions.test: (() => { const a = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d', { toneMapping: { mode: 'standard' } }).getContextAttributes(); return !!a.toneMapping && a.toneMapping.mode === 'standard'; })()

assertions.description: A mode outside CanvasToneMappingMode (e.g. the future-directions 'reinhard') throws a TypeError during dictionary conversion.
OffscreenCanvasRenderingContext2D honours the same setting: getContext('2d', {colorType: 'float16', toneMapping: {mode: 'extended'}}).getContextAttributes().toneMapping.mode === 'extended'.
assertions.test: (() => { const a = new OffscreenCanvas(4, 4).getContext('2d', { colorType: 'float16', toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' } }).getContextAttributes(); return !!a.toneMapping && a.toneMapping.mode === 'extended'; })()

assertions.description: A second getContext('2d', {toneMapping: {mode: 'extended'}}) on a canvas already created with 'standard' returns the same context and does not change its reported mode.
assertions.test: (() => { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); const a = c.getContext('2d', { toneMapping: { mode: 'standard' } }); const b = c.getContext('2d', { toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' } }); return a === b && b.getContextAttributes().toneMapping.mode === 'standard'; })()

assertions.description: The float16 bitmap that extended tone mapping displays can hold values above SDR white: color(srgb 3 0.5 0) reads back as red > 1 via getImageData({pixelFormat: 'rgba-float16'}).
assertions.test: (() => { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = c.height = 1; const x = c.getContext('2d', { colorType: 'float16', toneMapping: { mode: 'extended' } }); x.fillStyle = 'color(srgb 3 0.5 0)'; x.fillRect(0, 0, 1, 1); const d = x.getImageData(0, 0, 1, 1, { pixelFormat: 'rgba-float16' }); return d.pixelFormat === 'rgba-float16' && d.data[0] > 1; })()
